answer: The basalt test I would run is Registered choir member record with choral society attestation: concerts the society recorded across years of seasons, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that concerts the society recorded across years of seasons — so privacy survives, and the crystal is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the marble of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
